title: The Core Idea: Big-O & Efficient Thinking

scenes.say: Ever wonder why every interview starts with, 'What's the time complexity?' Let's break down why Big-O is the backbone of all data structures and algorithms.

scenes.label: Big-O
scenes.sub: Describes how runtime or space grows as input gets bigger.
scenes.say: Big-O tells you how your code scales as the data grows. It's not about exact speed, but how performance changes with size.
For example, arrays give you instant access. Linear search checks every item. Binary search halves the search space each time. Hash maps usually find things instantly.
Choosing the right structure matters. Arrays are great for fast lookup, but slow for inserts. Hash maps are fast for both, but need more memory.

scenes.question: Is O(n) always fast enough?
scenes.right: For huge data, even linear time can be slow. Always consider input size.
scenes.say: Here's the trap: just because something is linear time doesn't mean it's always fast enough. For massive data, even O(n) can be a dealbreaker.
